summary: Mauritius grants visa-free entry to a very broad list of nationalities — including the EU, UK and US — and issues free visas on arrival to most of the rest, with only a short list of passports needing a visa arranged before travel.

passportValidity.text: Mauritius only requires your passport to be valid for the whole of your intended stay, but some airlines apply a stricter six-month rule at check-in — more validity is safer.

source.name: Passport and Immigration Office, Mauritius — Travel Requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry requirement, but visitors use private clinics and costs add up — standard travel cover is recommended.

onwardTicket.text: You must hold a confirmed return or onward ticket — arriving without one can mean refused boarding or refused entry.

source.name: Passport and Immigration Office, Mauritius — Travel Requirements

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors should be able to show sufficient funds — commonly cited as USD 100 per person per day — together with confirmed accommodation for the stay.

declarations.name: Mauritius All-in-One Travel Form and Health Declaration Form
declarations.text: All passengers must complete the All-in-One Travel Form and the Health Declaration Form before boarding any aircraft or vessel bound for Mauritius, under the Quarantine (Health Declaration Form) Regulations 2026. The forms are free.

source.name: Passport and Immigration Office, Mauritius — Health and Entry Regulations

currencyLimits.text: Cash or bearer instruments worth MUR 500,000 or more (roughly USD 10,000) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Drug offenses carry severe penalties in Mauritius, even for small quantities.
Plants, fresh fruit, seeds and animal products require permits and must be declared to customs.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in hotels, restaurants and supermarkets across the island; keep some rupees for markets, street food, buses and taxis.

safety.text: Mauritius is one of Africa's safest destinations, with little serious crime. Petty theft around beaches and tourist areas is the main risk — do not leave valuables unattended — and swimmers should stay inside the lagoons, away from reef currents.

source.name: UK FCDO — Mauritius safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to December is cooler and drier — ideal beach and hiking weather; January to March is hot and humid, with cyclone risk.

tips.text: Remote workers, retirees and long-stay visitors can apply free of charge for the Premium Travel Visa, which allows stays of up to a year (renewable) while living on income earned outside Mauritius. Apply online before travel.

Cyclone season runs from November to April, peaking January to March. Mauritius has a well-drilled warning system (Class I–IV) — follow official bulletins and stay indoors during Class III and IV alerts.
Immigration asks where you are staying. Have your accommodation booking or host's details ready at the desk, along with your return ticket.
Swim inside the lagoons — currents beyond the reef are strong, and several popular beaches have no lifeguards. Heed local warnings about sea conditions.
Tap water is generally safe in most of the island, but after heavy rain or a cyclone stick to bottled or boiled water for a few days.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mauritius?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US and around a hundred other countries enter visa-free, and most remaining nationalities receive a free visa on arrival. Only a short list of passports must arrange a visa before traveling.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Mauritius as a tourist?
faq.answer: Visa-free visitors are normally admitted for up to 90 days (60 days for British citizens and most visa-on-arrival nationalities, two weeks for a few). The immigration officer sets the length of each stay on arrival. Tourist stays can be extended by the Passport and Immigration Office in Port Louis up to a maximum of 180 days in a calendar year, with proof of funds and accommodation.

faq.question: What is the Mauritius Premium Travel Visa?
faq.answer: A free long-stay visa aimed at remote workers, retirees and families who want to live in Mauritius for up to a year (renewable) while earning their income abroad. You apply online with proof of income, accommodation and insurance. It cannot be used to take up work in Mauritius itself.

faq.question: What do I need to show on arrival in Mauritius?
faq.answer: A passport valid for your stay, a confirmed return or onward ticket, the address of your accommodation and evidence of sufficient funds — commonly cited as USD 100 per person per day. Entry is normally granted for the length of your booking, up to your nationality's maximum.

faq.question: When is cyclone season in Mauritius?
faq.answer: November to April, with the highest risk from January to March. Direct hits are infrequent and hotels are built for storms, but flights and excursions can be disrupted — travel insurance that covers weather delays is worthwhile in those months.
